failures.criterion: A default-assignee pick made while an earlier save for the same project is out is superseded by the person's newest pick before it leaves the browser, so the stored default goes only from the in-flight pick to the newest one (the behaviour round 3's fix had and the issue's own assignee picker, useIssueFieldWrite, has; the architect asked the tester to decide whether sending every intermediate pick is acceptable).
failures.evidence: Judged a defect. At 4d93fbea every pick is its own scoped mutation, so every intermediate pick is sent and stored in turn. In Chromium against the real cmd/dispatch binary on PostgreSQL 17.11: with each save slowed 800 ms, six changes of mind 100 ms apart (bob, carol, dave, alice, bob, carol) sent six PUTs, and the server's default read bob, carol, dave, alice, bob, carol over 5.3 s while the control showed carol the whole time. A person arrowing through the closed picker with the keyboard makes a pick per key press: four ArrowDown presses with 500 ms saves sent alice, bob, carol and dave, and the stored default walked through all four over 2 s. Every stored pick is a default that an issue created in that moment is assigned to permanently (the chain runs only at create) and appends a settings.project_default_assignee.updated event, so a person who merely passed over someone can leave them assigned to work. The right behaviour: one save out per project, and a pick made while it is out replaces any pick already waiting, so when the save settles only the newest waiting pick is sent; keep the queue in QueryClient scope so a remounted row still waits behind the save in flight. Row 498's wire assertion ([bob, carol, alice]) pins the send-every-pick behaviour and needs [bob, alice] once carol is superseded by alice. Pinned by the red row `default assignee picks made while a save is out are superseded by the newest, so only it follows the save` (packages/dispatch/e2e/settings.e2e.ts:575, commit 9aa04afa2a0a): `cd packages/dispatch && DATABASE_URL=<a local Postgres> bun run e2e -- --project=chromium e2e/settings.e2e.ts -g 'superseded'` fails at :622, the wire carrying the extra `sent carol, answered carol, sent dave, answered dave`. The row passes with round 3's ProjectsSection.tsx (69bed70c74a4), so it asks for nothing new.

failures.criterion: A refused save is reported to the person who made it: a default-assignee save refused while Settings is not on screen is shown in that project's row when Settings is opened again.
failures.evidence: At 4d93fbea the row's error comes from its own useMutation observer, so it is lost when the row unmounts. In Chromium against the real server: stored alice, pick bob (save held), go to Inbox, the save is refused (500), come back to Settings -> the control shows alice and no alert, so nothing tells the person their pick was refused. With the row mounted, the same refusal shows the row's alert with Retry. Pinned by the red row `a default assignee save refused while Settings is left says so when Settings is reopened` (packages/dispatch/e2e/settings.e2e.ts:633, commit 9aa04afa2a0a): `bun run e2e -- --project=chromium e2e/settings.e2e.ts -g 'refused while Settings'` fails at :673, the alert carrying the server's error text is not found. The error can be read from the mutation cache the same way the pending pick is (useMutationState on the project's mutation key), up to the next attempt for that project.

errorCodeJudgement: The architect asked whether 400 INVALID_PROJECT misleads for a body without assignee. It does not: the repository's INVALID_<resource> codes name a bad body on a write to that resource (projects.go already answers INVALID_PROJECT for a project create with no name, and INVALID_ISSUE is the issue routes' body code), and the message names the missing field. Not a finding.
